planting.note: Marketed interchangeably with Tomahawk from the same high-alpha breeding line; give it maximum sun and a very tall, sturdy trellis since it is one of the most vigorous bittering bines available.

directions: A high-alpha American bittering workhorse, prized for pungent, dank, black-pepper aromatics alongside heavy resin production, and sold under both the Columbus and Tomahawk trade names depending on the grower. It is exceptionally vigorous, throwing long laterals that benefit from a wide, tall support structure and generous spacing. Full sun and rich, well-drained soil produce the heaviest cone set, and the plant tends to shrug off many diseases that trouble older bittering cultivars. Harvest once cones feel dry and papery, since delayed picking dulls the sharp resinous character brewers prize it for.
sources: John I. Haas, Inc. hop variety catalog

planting.note: A trademarked Yakima Valley release best known for candy-like tropical fruit notes; keep it in full sun with even moisture through cone development.

directions: El Dorado is a trademarked dual-purpose cultivar from the Yakima Valley whose cones deliver an unusually candy-sweet aroma of watermelon, pear, and stone fruit rather than the sharper citrus or resin notes typical of many American hops. Its moderate alpha acid content lets brewers use it for both late aroma additions and light bittering. The bine is moderately vigorous and benefits from a tall trellis and consistent watering during cone set, since drought stress can mute its fruit-forward character. Pick cones as soon as they feel light and papery to preserve the delicate aromatics.

planting.note: Bred in Tasmania and now grown internationally; it wants a long, warm growing season and full sun to develop its intense passionfruit aroma.

directions: Galaxy is an Australian aroma cultivar, released by Hop Products Australia from Perle-descended breeding stock, whose cones carry an intense passionfruit, citrus, and peach character that has made it one of the most sought-after hops in modern craft brewing. It performs best with a long, warm growing season and abundant sunshine, conditions that concentrate its essential oils. The bine is vigorous and cone-heavy, so plan on a very tall, sturdy trellis and rich, well-drained soil. Because its aroma is so concentrated, even modest late-addition or dry-hop rates produce a pronounced tropical fruit character in the finished beer.

planting.note: A trademarked release with an unusual sprawling growth habit; give it extra lateral space in addition to trellis height, and keep it in full sun.

directions: Sabro is a trademarked American cultivar prized for a distinctive aroma combining coconut, tangerine, and stone fruit unlike most other hop varieties. Unlike the typical single-leader climbing habit of most hops, Sabro throws unusually long lateral side-arms, so growers should provide extra horizontal space or a wider trellis in addition to standard vertical support. It is a relatively recent, fast-growing release that has become a favorite for hazy and tropical-style IPAs. Full sun, rich soil, and steady moisture during cone development help it reach its full aromatic potential.
sources: Hop Breeding Company / Yakima Chief Hops variety guide

planting.note: A trademarked dual-purpose hop with mango-forward aroma; full sun and a tall trellis suit its vigorous bine growth.

directions: Azacca is a trademarked dual-purpose American cultivar whose cones give off a distinctive mango and tropical citrus aroma alongside enough alpha acid to serve as a bittering addition when needed. The bine grows vigorously and produces heavy cone sets, so a tall, sturdy trellis and generous spacing pay off in yield. It tolerates full sun and average garden soil well, though like most hops it rewards consistent moisture during the summer growth push. Harvest promptly once cones dry and become papery to lock in its tropical fruit character before it fades.

planting.note: A public-domain release from Oregon State University's hop breeding program; grow it in full sun with a tall trellis for its dank, fruit-forward cones.

directions: Strata is a public cultivar released by Oregon State University's hop breeding program, known for a pungent, resinous aroma layered with notes of blackberry and passionfruit that has made it a favorite in hazy and West Coast-style IPAs. The bine shows good vigor and above-average disease tolerance compared with many aroma cultivars, making it a reasonably forgiving choice for home growers. It performs best in full sun on a tall, sturdy trellis with rich, well-drained soil. Because its aroma compounds are especially potent, brewers and home growers alike tend to use it in smaller quantities than older varieties.
sources: Oregon State University Extension — Hop Breeding Program

planting.note: Bred in Victoria, Australia; needs a long warm season and full sun similar to its Galaxy relative.

directions: Vic Secret is an Australian aroma cultivar developed by Hop Products Australia in Victoria state, producing cones with pronounced pineapple, pine, and passionfruit notes that pair well with Galaxy in modern hazy and Australian-style IPAs. It shares Galaxy's preference for a long, warm growing season and full sun exposure to fully express its aromatic oils. The bine is moderately vigorous and appreciates a tall trellis and well-drained, fertile soil. Harvest when cones are dry and lupulin-rich, since underripe cones give a noticeably weaker fruit character.

planting.note: A New Zealand aroma cultivar formerly called Stichbury's Seedling; prefers mild, maritime-influenced summers and full sun.

directions: Motueka is a New Zealand aroma cultivar, originally released under the name Stichbury's Seedling, bred from an open-pollinated Saaz-type seedling crossed with local wild hop stock, giving it bright lime, lemon, and tropical citrus aromatics unlike its noble-hop ancestor. Its comparatively low alpha acid content suits it mainly to late-kettle and dry-hop additions rather than bittering. The bine performs best in mild, maritime-influenced climates with consistent moisture and struggles in prolonged summer heat. Provide full sun, a tall trellis, and even watering through cone development to preserve its delicate citrus character.

planting.note: Bred by USDA-ARS as a hardier domestic substitute for Saaz-type noble hops; suits cooler, home-garden climates in full sun.

directions: Sterling is an American aroma cultivar released by the USDA-ARS breeding program specifically to give home and craft brewers a hardier, more disease-resistant substitute for true Saaz and other noble European hops, while retaining a similar mild, spicy, herbal-floral character. It establishes and yields more reliably than the finicky noble landraces, making it a good choice for gardeners in cooler climates who still want authentic lager and pilsner aromatics. Give it full sun, moderate consistent moisture, and a sturdy trellis for its climbing bines. Harvest when cones are dry and fragrant, and dry promptly to preserve its delicate spice-floral aroma.
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service — National Clonal Germplasm Repository, Hop Collection
Oregon State University Extension — Hop Cultivar Notes

planting.note: A USDA-ARS release with Hallertauer-derived aroma but easier home-garden vigor; give it full sun and steady moisture.

directions: Crystal is an American aroma cultivar released through USDA-ARS breeding trials, carrying Hallertauer-descended parentage that gives it a mild, floral, and spicy aroma reminiscent of German noble hops. Its lower alpha acid content makes it best suited to aroma and finishing additions rather than bittering. Compared with true European landraces it establishes and yields more reliably in home gardens, tolerating a wider range of soils and climates. Provide full sun, a tall support structure, and even moisture through summer to keep cone production and aroma quality consistent.
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service — National Clonal Germplasm Repository, Hop Collection

planting.note: A German cultivar bred from Northern Brewer parentage for improved disease resistance over true noble landraces; give it full sun and rich soil.

directions: Perle is a German aroma cultivar developed at the Hop Research Center in Hüll from Northern Brewer parentage, bred to offer a milder, spicy, minty aroma close to noble-hop character while resisting Verticillium wilt and other diseases far better than true landraces like Hallertauer Mittelfruh. It has since become a mainstay in both German and Pacific Northwest hop yards, valued for its dependable vigor. Full sun, deep fertile soil, and a tall, sturdy trellis suit its steady, moderately vigorous bine growth. It makes a good lower-maintenance substitute where authentic Hallertau proves too disease-prone for a home garden.
sources: Bavarian State Research Center for Agriculture (LfL)
